source: Raghav's Morning Yoga
Zainab started colouring at 04:25 p.m. and stopped at 05:10

items.question: Zainab started colouring at 04:25 p.m. and stopped at 05:10 p.m. (a) How long did she colour? Then: (b) How long is it from 07:20 a.m. to 10:50 a.m.?
steps: (a) Hop to the next whole hour. 04:25 p.m. to 05:00 p.m. is 60 − 25 = 35 minutes.
05:00 p.m. to 05:10 p.m. is 10 minutes.
35 + 10 = 45 minutes, so Zainab coloured for 45 minutes.
(b) Hop whole hours first. 07:20 a.m. to 10:20 a.m. is 10 − 7 = 3 hours.
So the time from 07:20 a.m. to 10:50 a.m. is 3 hours 30 minutes.
Check: 07:20 a.m. plus 3 hours is 10:20 a.m., and 10:20 a.m. plus 30 minutes is 10:50 a.m.

source: Zainab took 1 hour 50 minutes, Remo took 1 hour 25 minutes a

items.question: Zainab took 1 hour 50 minutes, Remo took 1 hour 25 minutes and Mary took 2 hours 5 minutes to finish a puzzle. Who took the longest time and who took the least?
steps: Compare the hours first. Zainab has 1 hour, Remo has 1 hour and Mary has 2 hours.
Mary has the most hours, so Mary took the longest time.
Zainab and Remo have the same hours, so compare their minutes.
25 minutes is less than 50 minutes, so Remo took less time than Zainab. Remo took the least time.
Check in minutes: Zainab 60 + 50 = 110, Remo 60 + 25 = 85 and Mary 120 + 5 = 125.
125 is the most and 85 is the least, so Mary is the longest and Remo is the least.
items.answer: Mary took the longest time and Remo took the least time

videos.answer: Mary took the longest time and Remo took the least time

source: Let us find out: Raghav's start time

items.question: Raghav practices yoga in the morning. At what time did Raghav start practising Yoga? ___
steps: Look at the first clock. The short blue hand is between 5 and 6, so the hour is 5.
The long orange hand is on 7. Each number on the dial is 5 minutes.
7 × 5 = 35 minutes.
The time is 05:35. Raghav practices yoga in the morning, so it is a.m.
Check: the hour hand is between 5 and 6, so the time is after 05:00 and before 06:00, and 05:35 is in that stretch.

source: Let us find out: Raghav's finish time

items.question: Raghav practices yoga in the morning. At what time did he finish? ___
steps: Look at the second clock. The short blue hand is just before 6, so the hour is 5.
The long orange hand is on 11. Each number on the dial is 5 minutes.
11 × 5 = 55 minutes.
The time is 05:55. It is the morning, so it is a.m.
Check: 55 minutes is 5 minutes short of 60, so the time is 5 minutes before 06:00, and the hour hand is almost on 6.

source: Let us find out: time spent on yoga

items.question: Raghav practices yoga in the morning. How much time did he spend practising Yoga? ___
steps: Raghav started at 05:35 a.m. and finished at 05:55 a.m.
Both times are in the same hour, 5, so take the smaller minutes from the bigger minutes.
55 − 35 = 20 minutes.
So Raghav spent 20 minutes on yoga.
Check: 05:35 a.m. plus 20 minutes is 05:55 a.m., because 35 + 20 = 55.

source: Let us find out: time elapsed

items.question: Find the time elapsed between the given time periods. Share your strategies. (a): 01:15 p.m. to 01:42 p.m.? (b): 03:18 p.m. to 08:18 p.m.? (c): 09:15 a.m. to 11:30 a.m.?
steps: (a): Both times are in the same hour, 1, so take the smaller minutes from the bigger minutes.
42 − 15 = 27 minutes.
(b): The minutes are the same, 18, so count the hours.
8 − 3 = 5 hours.
(c): Hop whole hours first. 09:15 a.m. to 11:15 a.m. is 11 − 9 = 2 hours.
11:15 a.m. to 11:30 a.m. is 30 − 15 = 15 minutes, so the answer to part (c) is 2 hours 15 minutes.
Share your strategy: you can hop to the next whole hour, or count the hours first. Another strategy may also work.
Check: 01:15 p.m. plus 27 minutes is 01:42 p.m., 03:18 p.m. plus 5 hours is 08:18 p.m., and 09:15 a.m. plus 2 hours 15 minutes is 11:30 a.m.
items.answer: (a): 27 minutes (b): 5 hours (c): 2 hours 15 minutes. Your strategy may differ.

videos.answer: (a): 27 minutes (b): 5 hours (c): 2 hours 15 minutes. Your strategy may differ.

source: Let us find out: time taken to paint a picture

items.question: The table below shows the time taken by 3 children to paint a picture. Raghav: 1 hour 20 minutes. Rani: 2 hours 10 minutes. Ritu: 1 hour 35 minutes. (a): Who took the longest time? (b): Who took the least time?
steps: Compare the hours first. Raghav has 1 hour, Rani has 2 hours and Ritu has 1 hour.
Rani has the most hours, so Rani took the longest time.
Raghav and Ritu both have 1 hour, so compare their minutes.
20 minutes is less than 35 minutes, so Raghav took the least time.
Check in minutes: Raghav 60 + 20 = 80, Rani 120 + 10 = 130 and Ritu 60 + 35 = 95. The most is 130 (Rani) and the least is 80 (Raghav).
items.answer: (a): Rani, 2 hours 10 minutes (b): Raghav, 1 hour 20 minutes

videos.answer: (a): Rani, 2 hours 10 minutes (b): Raghav, 1 hour 20 minutes

source: (a) Write 07:45 p.m. in the 24-hour format. (b) Write 16:20

items.question: (a) Write 07:45 p.m. in the 24-hour format. (b) Write 16:20 hours in the 12-hour format.
steps: (a) 07:45 p.m. is a p.m. time, so add 12 to the hour.
The minutes stay 45, so 07:45 p.m. is 19:45 hours.
(b) 16 is more than 12, so it is a p.m. time. Take 12 away from the hour.
The minutes stay 20, so 16:20 hours is 04:20 p.m.
Check: going back, 4 + 12 = 16 and 19 − 12 = 7, so both answers match.

source: A drawing class starts at 13:40 hours and ends at 16:15 hour

items.question: A drawing class starts at 13:40 hours and ends at 16:15 hours. How long does it last?
steps: 13:40 hours to 14:00 hours is 60 − 40 = 20 minutes.
14:00 hours to 16:00 hours is 16 − 14 = 2 hours.
16:00 hours to 16:15 hours is 15 minutes.
20 + 15 = 35 minutes.
So the drawing class lasts 2 hours 35 minutes.
Check: 13:40 hours plus 2 hours is 15:40 hours, and 15:40 hours plus 35 minutes is 16:15 hours.

source: Let us find out: the 12-hour and 24-hour table

items.question: Fill in the blanks by writing the time in the appropriate format. 12-hour format and 24-hour format: 05:30 a.m. = 05:30 hours; ___ = 08:35 hours; 11:55 a.m. = ___ hours; 02:30 p.m. = 14:30 hours; 05:30 p.m. = ___ hours; 09:35 p.m. = ___ hours.
steps: The rule: a morning time keeps its digits, and a p.m. time adds 12 to the hour. The minutes never change.
Second row: 08 is less than 12, so 08:35 hours is a morning time, 08:35 a.m.
Third row: 11:55 a.m. is a morning time, so it keeps its digits: 11:55 hours.
Fifth row: 05:30 p.m. is a p.m. time, so add 12 to the hour. 5 + 12 = 17, so it is 17:30 hours.
Sixth row: 09:35 p.m. is a p.m. time, so add 12 to the hour. 9 + 12 = 21, so it is 21:35 hours.
Check: going back, 17 − 12 = 5 and 21 − 12 = 9, so 17:30 hours is 05:30 p.m. and 21:35 hours is 09:35 p.m.
items.answer: Second row: 08:35 a.m. Third row: 11:55 hours. Fifth row: 17:30 hours. Sixth row: 21:35 hours.

videos.answer: Second row: 08:35 a.m. Third row: 11:55 hours. Fifth row: 17:30 hours. Sixth row: 21:35 hours.

source: Example 1: Raghu's trip to his Nana ji's house

items.question: Raghu left his house at 08:00 hours and arrived at his Nana ji's house at 09:05 hours. How long did he take to reach his house?
steps: Raghu left at 08:00 hours and arrived at 09:05 hours.
08:00 hours to 09:00 hours is 1 hour.
09:00 hours to 09:05 hours is 5 minutes.
So Raghu took 1 hour 5 minutes to reach his Nana ji's house.
Check: 08:00 hours plus 1 hour is 09:00 hours, and 09:00 hours plus 5 minutes is 09:05 hours.

source: In a race, Remo's time is 01:48 and Zainab's time is 01:52,

items.question: In a race, Remo's time is 01:48 and Zainab's time is 01:52, in minutes and seconds. Read each time. Who won, and by how many seconds? Change Remo's time to seconds.
steps: 01:48 means 1 minute 48 seconds. 01:52 means 1 minute 52 seconds.
Both took 1 minute, so compare the seconds. 48 is less than 52.
The least time wins, so Remo won.
52 − 48 = 4 seconds, so Remo won by 4 seconds.
1 minute = 60 seconds, so 1 minute 48 seconds = 60 + 48 = 108 seconds.
Check: Zainab's 1 minute 52 seconds is 60 + 52 = 112 seconds, and 112 − 108 = 4 seconds.
items.answer: Remo won by 4 seconds. His time, 1 minute 48 seconds, is 108 seconds

videos.answer: Remo won by 4 seconds. His time, 1 minute 48 seconds, is 108 seconds

source: Choose seconds or minutes for each activity: (a) tying a sho

items.question: Choose seconds or minutes for each activity: (a) tying a shoelace (b) boiling an egg (c) saying your name.
steps: Ask: is it over in less than 1 minute?
(a) Tying a shoelace is over in less than 1 minute, so the unit is seconds.
(b) Boiling an egg takes much longer than 1 minute, so the unit is minutes.
(c) Saying your name is over in less than 1 minute, so the unit is seconds.
Check: 1 minute is 60 seconds, and only boiling an egg takes longer than 60 seconds.

source: School Race: how much more than 1 minute

items.question: Akira, Sunita, and Mary are participating in a 200 m walking race. Each participant took 1 minute but how much more?
steps: The three boards on the winners' stand read 01:55, 01:56 and 01:57. These are minutes and seconds.
01:55 is 1 minute 55 seconds, so the child on stand 1 took 55 seconds more than 1 minute.
01:56 is 1 minute 56 seconds, so the child on stand 2 took 56 seconds more.
01:57 is 1 minute 57 seconds, so the child on stand 3 took 57 seconds more.
Check: 60 + 55 = 115, 60 + 56 = 116 and 60 + 57 = 117 seconds in all.
items.answer: 55, 56 and 57 seconds more than 1 minute, for the children on stands 1, 2 and 3

01:55 means 1 minute 55 seconds. 60 + 55 = 115 seconds.

source: Let Us Do (seconds or minutes)

items.question: Estimate whether you would take seconds or minutes to complete the following activities. Tick the appropriate cell. Activities: blinking of eyes; switching on and switching off the lights; counting from 1 to 20; filling a glass from the tap; melting of an ice-cube; making a phone call; sitting down on the floor; drinking a glass of water; snapping fingers; washing hands.
steps: The rule: if an activity is over in less than 1 minute, tick Seconds. If it takes longer than 1 minute, tick Minutes. This is an estimate.
Blinking of eyes is over in a moment: Seconds.
Switching on and switching off the lights: Seconds.
Counting from 1 to 20: Seconds.
Filling a glass from the tap: Seconds.
Melting of an ice-cube takes much longer than 1 minute: Minutes.
Making a phone call usually takes more than 1 minute: Minutes.
Sitting down on the floor, drinking a glass of water, snapping fingers and washing hands are each over in less than 1 minute: Seconds.
Check: 8 activities are in Seconds and 2 are in Minutes. This is a sample answer: your own estimate may differ, for example for washing hands.
items.answer: Sample answer. Seconds: eyes, lights, counting, tap, sitting, water, fingers, hands. Minutes: ice-cube, phone call. Your answer may differ

items.question: List events other than the ones listed above that you can do or that can happen in less than a minute or in a few seconds.

Things that happen: a bell ringing once, a ball dropping to the floor.
Check each one: is it over in less than 1 minute? If yes, keep it on the list.

items.question: Estimate and verify how many of these you can do in a minute. Activities: number of balloons blown; number of push-ups; number of breaths; number of hops on one leg.
steps: For each activity, first write your estimate: how many you think you can do in 1 minute.

source: Let Us Find: skipping the rope in 10 seconds

items.question: Find out the number of times you can skip the rope in 10 seconds.
steps: Ask a friend to watch the seconds hand. Begin when it is on 12 and stop when it is on 2.
From 12 to 2 is 2 × 5 = 10 seconds.
Count how many times you skip in that time.
Sample answer (practice values): 14 skips in 10 seconds.
In 1 minute there are 6 times 10 seconds, so you would skip about 14 × 6 = 84 times.
Check: 10 × 6 = 60, so 6 times 10 seconds is 1 minute. Your answer may differ.

source: Let Us Find: running 100 m

items.question: How long does it take you to run 100 m?
steps: Mark a start line and a finish line 100 m apart. Ask a friend to watch the seconds hand.
Start when the hand is on 12 and stop when you cross the finish line.
Sample answer (practice values): the hand went from 12 to 5, so 5 × 5 = 25 seconds.
If the hand goes past 12 again, one full round is 1 minute. For example, one full round and 10 more seconds is 1 minute 10 seconds.
Check: 25 seconds is less than 1 minute, so say it in seconds. Your answer may differ.
items.answer: Sample answer (practice values): 25 seconds. Your answer may differ

source: Remo timed himself tying his shoe. (a) The seconds hand star

items.question: Remo timed himself tying his shoe. (a) The seconds hand started on 3 and stopped on 8. How many seconds did he take? (b) On another try it started on 8 and stopped on 2. How many seconds?
steps: (a) Each number on the dial is 5 seconds. The start, 3, is 3 × 5 = 15 seconds. The stop, 8, is 8 × 5 = 40 seconds.
40 − 15 = 25 seconds.
(b) The start, 8, is 8 × 5 = 40 seconds. From 8 to 12 is 60 − 40 = 20 seconds.
From 12 to 2 is 2 × 5 = 10 seconds.
20 + 10 = 30 seconds.
Check: 40 seconds and 30 more is 70 seconds, and 70 − 60 = 10, which is the number 2.

source: The seconds hand is on 10. It runs for 25 seconds. Where doe

items.question: The seconds hand is on 10. It runs for 25 seconds. Where does it stop, and what happens to the minute hand?
steps: The hand starts on 10. Each number is 5 seconds, so 10 is 10 × 5 = 50 seconds.
50 + 25 = 75 seconds.
75 is more than 60, so the hand has gone past 12 once. 75 − 60 = 15 seconds.
15 seconds is 15 ÷ 5 = 3, so the hand stops on 3.
The hand went past 12 once, so the minute hand has moved on by one mark.
Check: from 10 to 12 is 10 seconds and from 12 to 3 is 15 seconds, and 10 + 15 = 25 seconds.
items.answer: The seconds hand stops on 3, and the minute hand moves on by one mark

videos.answer: The seconds hand stops on 3, and the minute hand moves on by one mark

source: (a) Change 5 hours 25 minutes to minutes. (b) Change 370 min

items.question: (a) Change 5 hours 25 minutes to minutes. (b) Change 370 minutes to hours and minutes.
steps: (a) 1 hour = 60 minutes, so 5 hours = 5 × 60 = 300 minutes.
(b) 60 × 6 = 360 and 60 × 7 = 420. 370 is between them, so there are 6 whole hours.
370 − 360 = 10 minutes are left.
So 370 minutes = 6 hours 10 minutes.

source: (a) Change 4 minutes 30 seconds to seconds. (b) Change 400 s

items.question: (a) Change 4 minutes 30 seconds to seconds. (b) Change 400 seconds to minutes and seconds.
steps: (a) 1 minute = 60 seconds, so 4 minutes = 4 × 60 = 240 seconds.
(b) 60 × 6 = 360 and 60 × 7 = 420. 400 is between them, so there are 6 whole minutes.
400 − 360 = 40 seconds are left.
So 400 seconds = 6 minutes 40 seconds.

source: Let Us Do (changing units), Q1 (a)

items.question: Use the double number line below to complete the conversions. Hours: 1 hour, ___, 4 hours, 7 hours, ___, 9 hours, ___, ___. Minutes: 60 minutes, 120 minutes, ___, ___, 480 minutes, ___, 660 minutes, 720 minutes.
steps: Each tick is one number of hours, and the minutes below it are 60 times as many.
Above 120 minutes: 120 ÷ 60 = 2 hours. The × 2 arrow joins 1 hour to 2 hours.
Below 4 hours: 4 × 60 = 240 minutes.
Below 7 hours: 7 × 60 = 420 minutes.
Above 480 minutes: 480 ÷ 60 = 8 hours.
Below 9 hours: 9 × 60 = 540 minutes.
Above 660 minutes: 660 ÷ 60 = 11 hours. Above 720 minutes: 720 ÷ 60 = 12 hours.
Check: every number of minutes is 60 times its number of hours.

source: Let Us Do (changing units), Q1 (b)

items.question: Do as instructed. You can use the above double number line for the following conversions. (i): 1 hour 10 minutes = ___ minutes (ii): 2 hours 45 minutes = ___ minutes (iii): 3 hours 15 minutes = ___ minutes (iv): 4 hours 20 minutes = ___ minutes (v): 75 minutes = ___ hour ___ minutes (vi): 150 minutes = ___ hours ___ minutes (vii): 220 minutes = ___ hours ___ minutes (viii): 390 minutes = ___ hours ___ minutes
steps: (i): 1 hour = 60 minutes, so 1 hour 10 minutes is 60 + 10 = 70 minutes.
(ii): 2 hours = 2 × 60 = 120 minutes, and 120 + 45 = 165 minutes.
(iii): 3 hours = 3 × 60 = 180 minutes, and 180 + 15 = 195 minutes.
(iv): 4 hours = 4 × 60 = 240 minutes, and 240 + 20 = 260 minutes.
(v): 75 minutes: 60 minutes make 1 hour, and 75 − 60 = 15 minutes are left. So 1 hour 15 minutes.
(vi): 150 minutes: 60 × 2 = 120, and 150 − 120 = 30 minutes are left. So 2 hours 30 minutes.
(vii): 220 minutes: 60 × 3 = 180, and 220 − 180 = 40 minutes are left. So 3 hours 40 minutes.
(viii): 390 minutes: 60 × 6 = 360, and 390 − 360 = 30 minutes are left. So 6 hours 30 minutes.
items.answer: (i): 70; (ii): 165; (iii): 195; (iv): 260 minutes. (v): 1 hour 15 minutes; (vi): 2 hours 30 minutes; (vii): 3 hours 40 minutes; (viii): 6 hours 30 minutes

steps: (i): 60 × 5 = 300, and 320 − 300 = 20 seconds are left. So 5 minutes 20 seconds.
(ii): 60 × 3 = 180, and 225 − 180 = 45 seconds are left. So 3 minutes 45 seconds.
(iii): 60 × 11 = 660, and 700 − 660 = 40 seconds are left. So 11 minutes 40 seconds.
(iv): 60 × 16 = 960, and 1,000 − 960 = 40 seconds are left. So 16 minutes 40 seconds.

items.question: Raghav studies Mathematics, English, Hindi, and The World Around Us subjects. He took 50 minutes to study each of the subjects. Find the total time taken in hours and minutes. Share your strategies with your class.
steps: There are 4 subjects and each took 50 minutes.
4 × 50 = 200 minutes.
60 × 3 = 180 minutes, which is 3 hours, and 200 − 180 = 20 minutes are left.
So the total time is 3 hours 20 minutes.
Another strategy: 50 + 50 = 100 minutes is 1 hour 40 minutes for 2 subjects, and 1 hour 40 minutes twice is 2 hours 80 minutes, which is 3 hours 20 minutes.
Check: 3 × 60 + 20 = 200 minutes.
items.answer: 3 hours 20 minutes. Your strategy may differ

items.question: Zainab starts painting at 03:20 p.m. and paints for 1 hour 50 minutes. At what time does she stop?
steps: Add the hours first: 03:20 p.m. plus 1 hour is 04:20 p.m.
From 04:20 p.m. to 05:00 p.m. is 60 − 20 = 40 minutes.
50 − 40 = 10 minutes are left to add.
05:00 p.m. plus 10 minutes is 05:10 p.m.
So Zainab stops at 05:10 p.m.
Check by going back: 05:10 p.m. minus 1 hour is 04:10 p.m., and 04:10 p.m. minus 50 minutes is 03:20 p.m.

items.question: Remo finished reading at 08:15 p.m. He read for 2 hours 40 minutes. At what time did he start?
steps: Go back the hours first: 08:15 p.m. minus 2 hours is 06:15 p.m.
From 06:15 p.m. back to 06:00 p.m. is 15 minutes.
40 − 15 = 25 minutes are left to go back.
06:00 p.m. minus 25 minutes is 05:35 p.m.
So Remo started at 05:35 p.m.
Check by going forward: 05:35 p.m. plus 2 hours is 07:35 p.m., and 07:35 p.m. plus 40 minutes is 08:15 p.m.

items.question: (a) A bus leaves at 10:40 a.m. and the trip takes 3 hours 30 minutes. When does it arrive? (b) A train leaves at 10:15 p.m. and the journey takes 5 hours 45 minutes. When does it arrive?
steps: (a) 10:40 a.m. is a morning time, so it is 10:40 hours.
10:40 hours plus 3 hours is 13:40 hours.
From 13:40 hours to 14:00 hours is 20 minutes, and 30 − 20 = 10 minutes are left, so 14:10 hours.
14 − 12 = 2, so 14:10 hours is 02:10 p.m. The clock passed 12 noon, so a.m. changed to p.m.
(b) 10:15 p.m. is 10 + 12 = 22, so it is 22:15 hours.
22:15 hours plus 5 hours is 27:15 hours. 27:15 hours plus 45 minutes is 28:00 hours, because 15 + 45 = 60 minutes make 1 more hour.
A day ends at 24:00 hours, so take 24 away: 28 − 24 = 4. The train arrives at 04:00 hours, which is 04:00 a.m. the next day.
Check: 10:15 p.m. to midnight is 1 hour 45 minutes, and midnight to 04:00 a.m. is 4 hours. 1 hour 45 minutes plus 4 hours is 5 hours 45 minutes.

items.question: Jyoti went to play at 06:15 PM. She came back after 1 hour 45 minutes. At what time did she reach home?
steps: Add the hours first: 06:15 PM plus 1 hour is 07:15 PM.
From 07:15 PM to 08:00 PM is 60 − 15 = 45 minutes, and 45 minutes is all the minutes to add.
So 07:15 PM plus 45 minutes is 08:00 PM.
Check by going back: 08:00 PM minus 1 hour is 07:00 PM, and 07:00 PM minus 45 minutes is 06:15 PM.

source: Let Us Do (time problems), Q5

items.question: Ragini took 1 hour 10 minutes to do her homework. She finished it at 09:40 PM. What time did she start?
steps: Go back the hours first: 09:40 PM minus 1 hour is 08:40 PM.
Go back the 10 minutes: 08:40 PM minus 10 minutes is 08:30 PM.
So Ragini started at 08:30 PM.
Check by going forward: 08:30 PM plus 1 hour is 09:30 PM, and 09:30 PM plus 10 minutes is 09:40 PM.

items.question: A group of children left for a picnic at 08:30 AM. They returned after 4 hours and 10 minutes. At what time did they return?
steps: Add the hours first: 08:30 AM plus 4 hours is 12:30 PM. The clock passes 12 noon, so AM changes to PM.
Add the 10 minutes: 12:30 PM plus 10 minutes is 12:40 PM.
So the children returned at 12:40 PM.
Check in 24-hour time: 08:30 hours plus 4 hours 10 minutes is 12:40 hours, and 12:40 hours is 12:40 PM.

source: Let Us Do (time problems), Q7

items.question: Raji started her homework at 06:00 PM. She finished her homework in 1 hour 30 minutes. At what time did she finish?
steps: Add the hours first: 06:00 PM plus 1 hour is 07:00 PM.
Add the 30 minutes: 07:00 PM plus 30 minutes is 07:30 PM.
So Raji finished at 07:30 PM.
Check by going back: 07:30 PM minus 1 hour 30 minutes is 06:00 PM.

items.question: Alya goes out to play at 05:30 PM and comes back after 1 hour 10 minutes. At what time does she come back?
steps: Add the hours first: 05:30 PM plus 1 hour is 06:30 PM.
Add the 10 minutes: 06:30 PM plus 10 minutes is 06:40 PM.
So Alya comes back at 06:40 PM.
Check by going back: 06:40 PM minus 1 hour is 05:40 PM, and 05:40 PM minus 10 minutes is 05:30 PM.

items.question: If the lunch break of a school starts at 12:30 PM and ends in 35 minutes, what time will lunch end?
steps: From 12:30 PM to 01:00 PM is 30 minutes.
35 − 30 = 5 minutes are left to add.
01:00 PM plus 5 minutes is 01:05 PM. On the 12-hour clock, after 12:59 the time goes to 01:00.
So the lunch break ends at 01:05 PM.
Check in 24-hour time: 12:30 hours plus 35 minutes is 13:05 hours, and 13 − 12 = 1, so 01:05 PM.

source: Let Us Do (time problems), Q10

items.question: It is 08:35 PM right now. What time will it be after 8 hours and 25 minutes?
steps: 08:35 PM is a p.m. time, so add 12 to the hour: 8 + 12 = 20, and it is 20:35 hours.
Add the 25 minutes first: 20:35 hours plus 25 minutes is 21:00 hours.
Add the 8 hours: 21:00 hours plus 8 hours is 29:00 hours.
A day ends at 24:00 hours, so take 24 away: 29 − 24 = 5. The time is 05:00 hours the next day.
05:00 hours is a morning time, so it is 05:00 AM the next day.
Check: 08:35 PM to midnight is 3 hours 25 minutes, and midnight to 05:00 AM is 5 hours. 3 hours 25 minutes plus 5 hours is 8 hours 25 minutes.
